sites.downstream: Extracted <selection> tag used as dict key into support_routes to select handler; extracted <reasoning> tag printed to stdout as diagnostic
sites.reason: Routing decision is a closed-set Choice over 4 options (billing, technical, account, product) from benign fixtures, but the same call also generates <reasoning> text printed to stdout. The decision component fits Jev Choice; the reasoning output is observable generation that changes stdout behavior if removed. Classified MIXED per audit rules: a router that returns and prints explanatory reasoning is MIXED even if only its route controls execution.

options.benefit: Jev Choice is ~100ms and significantly cheaper than a Sonnet call for the routing decision. Expected cost = Jev cost + fallback fraction * original cost. Most clear-cut support tickets would resolve at high confidence.
options.risk: Site is MIXED, not pure DECISION. Reasoning diagnostic text changes format on Jev path (synthetic vs LLM-generated). Conservative posture retains fallback, so worst case is added Jev latency before original call on low-confidence inputs. Scoped to demo fixtures, not validated for adversarial production input.

options.benefit: Cleanly separates the DECISION from the GENERATION. Routing decision gets Jev speed/cost advantages. Reasoning can be made optional or logged at a different level.
options.risk: Two calls instead of one on Jev path if reasoning is always generated. More complex code. Changes observable behavior if reasoning generation is skipped or uses a different model.

options.benefit: No integration risk. No new dependency. No behavior change.

sites.downstream: Return value of route() function — free-form prose support response
sites.reason: Produces free-form prose support responses. Jev is not trained for text generation. Generation is never Jev-only.

options.benefit: Correct tool for the job. No risk.
